source: Bhushan, Zhang, Wang (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks
finding: First rubric that scores LLM agent steps on Boden's modes, 0 Routine to 4 Transformational. A change of representation, objective, modality or task definition scores 4. Human annotators and an LLM judge both used it.
numbers: 3 trained annotators labelled 300 episodes, Krippendorff alpha 0.724 (ordinal). GPT-5 judge vs humans Spearman 0.732 (full prompt); 0.684 without examples; 0.699 without edge rules; 0.712 without procedure.
limits: Rubric scores are relative to the agent's own prior episodes (P-creativity), so level 4 is relative, not historical. Only ML-engineering tasks. Transformational is not reported separately.
agent_relevance: A checkable trigger list for O4/O6: did the step change representation, objective, modality or task definition? A code-checkable label, not an opinion.

source: Bhushan, Zhang, Wang (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks (judge validity)
finding: A strong LLM judge tracks human novelty ratings better than embeddings or concept sets. Judge quality scales with model size. Bias tests found no length or self-preference problem.
numbers: Embedding nearest-neighbour 0.637, centroid 0.589, mean 0.503, graph edit -0.329. Concept fuzzy 0.539, set 0.508. Open judges: GLM-5 0.703, DeepSeek V3.2 0.700, Qwen3-235B 0.685, GPT-OSS-120B 0.544. GPT-5 scored Qwen episodes +0.300 above a neutral judge but its own only +0.129 (p=0.000038), so no self-favouring.
limits: Judge sees all prior episodes, so cost grows with run length. Agreement with humans is moderate, not near 1. G5 says a judge may be used only blind.
agent_relevance: If a judge must score a reframe, use a strong model with the full rubric and prior-attempt context. Embedding distance alone is a weaker proxy (0.50-0.64).

source: Bhushan, Zhang, Wang (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks (exploration decays)
finding: Every agent, human or LLM, becomes less novel each episode as it moves from exploring to refining. LLM agents decay faster and further than Kaggle humans. Greedy search starts most novel and falls steeply.
numbers: 10 MLE-Bench tasks; AIDE with GPT-5 and Qwen3-32B, 8 runs per task; AIRA-Dojo MCTS 8 runs per task; Greedy and Evolutionary 4 runs on 3 tasks; max 10 episodes, 8 hours. All three AIRA strategies fell below P-creativity 1 within a few episodes. Behaviour mix: strategic exploration about 75% early, about 25% at the end; parametric refinement 15% to over 50%; bug fixing 5% to 25%.
limits: Small episode count (10). Humans compared are not top performers.
agent_relevance: Nothing in a plain loop returns the agent to reframing once refinement starts. A stalled-refinement detector in code should be what opens O4 (fits G1).

source: Bhushan, Zhang, Wang (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks (novelty not linked to gains)
finding: Changes in novelty and changes in score are unrelated, in agents and in humans. Agents find new regions but do not turn them into better scores.
numbers: Spearman of change in impact vs change in P-creativity: Humans -0.111 (p<0.05), AIDE GPT-5 -0.021, AIDE Qwen +0.056, AIRA Qwen -0.026. GPT-5 H-creativity 1.423 vs gold-medal humans 0.744 (p<1e-15); Qwen configs 0.838 and 0.800, not different from gold. Only 21.25% of GPT-5 runs and 10.85% of AIDE Qwen runs reached medal level. Human H-creativity rises with medal tier: gold 0.744, silver 0.524, bronze 0.293.
limits: Human medal data is post-competition notebooks. Novelty is measured against a public Kaggle corpus.
agent_relevance: Novelty is not a goal by itself. Any rule-changing move needs a held-out check (G3) before it is kept.

source: Bhushan, Zhang, Wang (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks (after a novel state)
finding: After reaching a novel approach, agents refine it and do not gain. They also do not drop it when it is poor. No signal tells them a paradigm has a ceiling.
numbers: 92 episodes in top 20% H-creativity and bottom 20% impact: 87.0% (80/92) went to REFINE; 53.8% of refined episodes lost novelty next episode, median impact change 0.000; ABANDON rate 6.5% for low-impact episodes vs 16.4% for high-impact. Case run: the same accuracy repeated six consecutive episodes. Cross-task control: wrong-task code scored 2.39 vs 1.42 / 0.84 / 0.80 for in-task agents, so novelty is task-directed.
limits: Case analysis of a subset; descriptive.
agent_relevance: Supports a plateau detector (same score K times) as the code signal for O4/O6, and a rule to drop a novel but unhelpful branch.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) InnoGym: Benchmarking the Innovation Potential of AI Agents
finding: Benchmark with two scores per solution: performance gain over the best known solution, and methodological novelty. Agents often had novelty without gain. Robustness limited gains.
numbers: 18 tasks; 3 agent frameworks. No agent beat the best human solution on any task. On CDML and PTTALC, all agents failed to produce a valid solution. MLab led on both gain and novelty. On RCIC and TrojanDetection, mid-to-high novelty went with some of the lowest scores.
limits: Novelty is distance in solution space, not change of the rules of the space. Few runs (3 per setting).
agent_relevance: Separates conceptual innovation (high novelty, equal score) from breakthrough (both). A reframe that reaches the same score by a different method is worth recording.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) InnoGym: Benchmarking the Innovation Potential of AI Agents (temperature and base model)
finding: Sampling temperature trades gain against novelty. A mid range keeps most of the performance and raises novelty. Base model strength mattered more than agent framework.
numbers: Gain highest at low temperature, novelty rises with temperature; sweet spot 0.5 to 0.75 (3 runs). Scores on CirclePacking: Gemini-2.5-Pro 2.49, GPT-5 2.44, DeepSeek-v3.1 2.40, AlphaEvolve 2.65.
limits: Single task for the model comparison; temperature sweep on few tasks.
agent_relevance: Cheap spread knob for O8 candidate generation: moderate temperature, not high.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Machine Creativity via Self-Evolving Challenges
finding: Code benchmark built on Boden. It covers only combinatorial and exploratory creativity. Transformational creativity is left out. Score is quality times novelty, with runnable code separating creativity from nonsense.
numbers: Human check: 89.1% instance validity; Spearman 0.78 between automated and human creativity rankings.
limits: No transformational subset. Novelty is logic distance from reference solutions.
agent_relevance: There is no standard benchmark for transformational tasks in code. Any test of O4/O6 will be our own.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Machine Creativity via Self-Evolving Challenges (scale and reasoning)
finding: Larger models gain in correctness and in combining, but not in exploring (convergence by scaling). Reasoning mode helps constraint-driven exploration and not cross-domain combination.
numbers: Scaling raises Pass@1 while novelty falls or plateaus. Reasoning gives almost no benefit on combination tasks and a significant benefit on exploration tasks. A steering vector (EvoRePE) raised Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct creativity on the Combo set from 0.174 to 0.192 with AlphaEvolve.
limits: Open-weight models for the steering part; gain of 0.018 is small. Metric tied to the benchmark.
agent_relevance: More thinking helps when the space has explicit constraints, the setting for O4 (relax one constraint). It does not widen the space by itself.

source: Beaty et al. (2026) AGC-Bench: Measuring Artificial General Creativity
finding: Systematic review plus meta-benchmark of 78 datasets. One general creativity factor across 83 frontier LLMs, related to but separate from reasoning and knowledge. Transformational creativity is named as not covered.
numbers: 3,101 papers screened, 497 benchmarks; factor C explains 81.5% of variance, omega 0.96; correlation with fluid reasoning rho 0.55 (n=82), MMLU-Pro 0.62 (n=57), Williams t 0.04 p 0.96; parameters vs composite rho 0.69 (42 open models). Judge trained on 48,299 corrected ratings.
limits: Mostly text, English; judged by LLMs after leniency correction. Transformational creativity not assessed. Scores are cohort-specific.
agent_relevance: Creativity is not the same as reasoning, so a reasoning scaffold alone will not give it. Supports a separate operator rather than more chain of thought.

source: Beaty et al. (2026) AGC-Bench: Measuring Artificial General Creativity (instruction vs reasoning)
finding: Telling models to be creative moves creative scores far more than turning on reasoning. The effect did not cost validity.
numbers: 'Be creative' vs 'be effective' on 18 frontier models: dz +1.40 (length-residualised); 99.4% of 2,700 generations passed a 3-judge validity gate. Reasoning on vs baseline, 10 other models: dz +0.34, about one quarter as large. Top human still above top LLM on five matched tasks.
limits: Different model cohorts for the two tests. Effects are on creative-writing-style tasks, not rule change.
agent_relevance: An explicit divergence instruction is cheap and large for O8, but G1 says do not use it on a schedule.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Blind expert review found LLM-written research ideas more novel than expert ideas and slightly less feasible. A human reranker raised novelty a little more.
numbers: 49 idea writers, 79 reviewers, 298 unique reviews, 7 topics. Novelty: human 4.84, AI 5.64 (p<0.05), AI plus human rerank 5.81.
limits: Ideas only, not executed. LLM ideas were filtered from a large pool.
agent_relevance: Novel-sounding output is easy to get. Value is the open question (see next lines).

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers (diversity collapse)
finding: Overgenerating ideas does not give diverse ideas: duplicates pile up. LLM self-evaluation as a ranker was unreliable.
numbers: Out of 4000 generated seed ideas, only about 200 were non-duplicate (cosine similarity threshold 0.8, about 5%). Share of non-duplicates in new batches kept falling; accumulated unique ideas plateaued.
limits: Embedding threshold 0.8 chosen by manual check; one pipeline.
agent_relevance: Sampling more from one model is a weak way to leave a conceptual space (G4). A structural change is needed.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
finding: Follow-up that executed the ideas. LLM ideas lost much more score after real execution than human ideas, closing and partly flipping the novelty advantage.
numbers: 43 experts each spent over 100 hours on an idea; blind review of 4-page papers. Change after execution (1-10 scale): human ideas novelty -0.010, excitement +0.078, effectiveness -0.052; AI ideas novelty -1.049, excitement -1.760, effectiveness -1.879 (gap p<0.05 on all four metrics). After execution: excitement 3.90 AI vs 4.48 human; effectiveness 4.13 vs 4.78 (ranking flips, not significant, N=43). Pre- and post-execution scores correlate weakly; moderately negative for AI excitement.
limits: Small sample; flip not significant; one field (NLP prompting research); one idea generator.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct evidence that idea-stage novelty does not predict value. Fits G3: a new frame counts only after it is run on something it was not fitted to.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
finding: Claimed that many LLMs give near-identical open-ended answers within and across models. Read as evidence that models stay inside one conceptual space.
numbers: 26K real open-ended queries; 70+ models; 31,250 human annotations (25 per example). 50 responses per query at temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9: in 79% of cases mean pairwise similarity exceeded 0.8. Random pairs from the global pool fell in 0.1-0.2.
limits: The paper itself says its random-pair reference is not a matched baseline. See the reanalysis next.
agent_relevance: If models share one space, several samples from one model or from several models will not give new frames (G4).

source: Schaeffer et al. (2026) How Strong Is the Evidence for the Artificial Hivemind?
finding: Reanalysis finds the flagship example and the similarity threshold do not hold up as stated. Prompting raised diversity, against the original's claim that inference-time fixes are inadequate. The authors do not say the effect is absent.
numbers: Time-metaphor example: 'river' in 80.5% of 750 responses, next vehicle 18.4%, 14 vehicles above the retention bar, not two clusters. With a same-prompt null, original same-prompt pairs exceed 0.8 two to three times as often as different-idea pairs, so some effect remains. No human baseline in the original. Min-p sampling did not raise diversity.
limits: Authors say they do not resolve whether the Hivemind is real. Their own test used one prompt set and one embedding model.
agent_relevance: Treat 'LLMs are homogeneous' as partly true and measurement-dependent. Prompt-level changes can still shift diversity. Do not build on the strong claim.

source: Ord (2024) Interpolation, Extrapolation, Hyperpolation: Generalising into new dimensions
finding: Defines hyperpolation: estimating a function outside the subspace of the data. Links it to Boden's transformational creativity (altering, adding or deleting dimensions) and argues current ML is weak at it.
numbers: No experiment. Argument that learning problems are built so that data lie on a manifold and queries stay near it.
limits: Conceptual paper. No measured LLM result.
agent_relevance: A clear operational reading of O4: add a dimension the examples never varied, then ask what follows. Not shown to be doable by a prompt.

source: Franceschelli, Musolesi (2026) On the Creativity of AI Agents
finding: Argues LLM agents show functional creativity (interpolation and extrapolation), not transformational creativity, which would need hyperpolation. Says testing for transformational creativity is open and maybe unsolvable. Tool-making agents can add actions, but a probabilistic model writes them.
numbers: No new data. Mentions superspace extrapolation (Lucas, Sterling, Kemp 2012) as a possible test, and says designing such tasks is itself a transformational task.
limits: Position paper; claims about what LLMs cannot do are asserted, not tested.
agent_relevance: Suggests testing O4 by adding a dimension to a known rule set and checking whether outputs use it. We must build the tests.

source: Franceschelli, Musolesi (2023, v5 2025) On the Creativity of Large Language Models
finding: Argues LLMs can at most reach combinatorial or exploratory creativity, because they follow the training distribution and RLHF makes text less diverse. Says outputs look creative to users through B-novelty (new to the beholder).
numbers: No new data. Cites reduced diversity after preference tuning (Kirk et al. 2024).
limits: A 2023 prediction kept in later versions; not tested against later reasoning models.
agent_relevance: A claim to test, not a finding. The B-novelty point warns that a user's sense of novelty is not a measure.

source: Schapiro, Black, Varshney (2025) Transformational Creativity in Science: A Graphical Theory (ICCC 2025)
finding: Formal model of a conceptual space as a dependency graph of rules over axioms. Proves that changing an axiom has the most transformative potential, since everything that depends on it changes. Fits Copernicus, non-Euclidean geometry, relativity.
numbers: Theory and worked cases (Ptolemaic to heliocentric, Euclidean to non-Euclidean, Newtonian to relativistic). No experiments.
limits: Short paper; no empirical test; cases chosen after the fact.
agent_relevance: Gives O4 a procedure: list assumptions, find the one with most dependents, vary that one. Cheap to code. Untested.

source: Same paper: prior formalisations of transformation (Wiggins 2006; Ritchie 2006; Santo, Wiggins, Cardoso 2024; Toivanen 2018), as described by Schapiro et al.
finding: Wiggins treats transformation as search over the space of generative systems; Ritchie as modification of the conceptual structure; Santo et al. as a shift of the hypothesis space from new data in formal learning theory; Toivanen et al. as meta-level modules that change constraints in a song generator.
numbers: Secondary description only; I did not open the four originals.
limits: Wording is from the citing authors and not checked against the originals.
agent_relevance: Four formal routes to O4/O6; the meta-level constraint-editing design is the closest to a scaffold.

source: Cross-check: no benchmark covers transformational creativity
finding: Three 2026 sources (AGC-Bench, CreativeBench, Franceschelli and Musolesi) each say the transformational mode is not measured. Only the ML-engineering rubric includes it, as a level-4 label.
numbers: 78 datasets in AGC-Bench; 2 subsets in CreativeBench (Combo, Explore); 5-level rubric in Bhushan et al.
limits: Based on my reading of these papers, not a search of all work.
agent_relevance: No outside measurement exists to calibrate O4/O6. Plan our own tests with held-out checks.

source: Cross-check: novelty and value come apart across studies
finding: Several studies agree LLM novelty does not give value without a check: Si 2025 execution study, Bhushan 2026, InnoGym 2026, CreativeBench 2026 (more correct but less divergent when scaled). None of the opened studies shows the reverse.
numbers: Si: execution drops of 1.05 to 1.88 points on a 10-point scale for AI ideas vs about 0 for human; Bhushan: correlations -0.111 to +0.056.
limits: Different tasks and different novelty measures; no common scale.
agent_relevance: A reframe should be kept only if it survives a held-out check, never because it looks new.

source: Cross-check: cheap levers that move novelty
finding: Two cheap levers move novelty: asking for creativity (dz +1.40) and mid-range temperature (0.5 to 0.75 best trade). Reasoning mode alone adds little (dz +0.34 overall; none for combination).
numbers: Values from AGC-Bench, InnoGym and CreativeBench.
limits: Effects are on novelty of output, not on rule change.
agent_relevance: For O8 spread, use an instruction plus moderate temperature, and count duplicates (Si: about 5% unique at scale).

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind (human-rating part)
finding: Models, reward models and LLM judges agree less with humans on answers where human annotators disagree with each other (idiosyncratic taste), even when overall quality is similar.
numbers: 31,250 human annotations, 25 independent ratings per example; exact calibration figures not recorded from the abstract and intro read.
limits: Only the abstract-level claim was recorded here; the rater-disagreement metrics were not checked in detail.
agent_relevance: A judge of whether a reframe is good is weakest exactly where taste splits, so rely on code checks (G5) for those cases.
